reason: Full text read; in scope as typed experience pool inside a TKGQA system; harness-RSI contribution secondary.

paper.title: MemoTime: Memory-Augmented Temporal Knowledge Graph Enhanced Large Language Model Reasoning
paper.central_claim: MemoTime, a training-free memory-augmented TKG reasoning framework (Tree of Time decomposition, operator-aware retrieval, self-evolving experience memory), achieves state-of-the-art temporal QA and lets small LLMs approach large ones.

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref not exposed to the worker; model_type is the controller-assigned type.

rationale: Weak-fit in scope: TKGQA pipeline with a secondary experience memory; single memory ablation, split/gate unreported, no stats, inconsistent tables.

evidence.quote: a self-evolving experience memory stores verified reasoning traces, toolkit decisions, and sub-question embeddings for cross-type reuse.
evidence.support_explanation: Memory component relevant to harness RSI.

evidence.quote: They often rely on manually crafted or static exemplars, which are costly to construct and insufficiently generalizable across diverse temporal question types,
evidence.support_explanation: Author gap for the memory part.

evidence.quote: At each node, MemoTime first checks whether a similar reasoning trace exists in the experience pool for direct reuse.
evidence.support_explanation: Read path: memory lookup before tool use.

evidence.quote: A sub-question is considered sufficient when one or more candidate paths provide consistent evidence aligned with its indicator.
evidence.support_explanation: Write gate is an LLM sufficiency judgment (no gold label stated).

evidence.quote: New entries are inserted into both the global memory and the buffer; obsolete or low-value traces are periodically pruned to prevent redundancy.
The memory layer continuously re-weights and reorganizes stored exemplars based on retrieval frequency, temporal freshness, and reasoning success.
The incorrect samples are used as warnings.
evidence.support_explanation: Implies labels or judge verdicts for failures; source not stated.

evidence.quote: All experiences are dynamically learned from verified reasoning traces, with five predefined exemplars used for cold-start initialization.
evidence.support_explanation: Cold start 5 exemplars; which questions populate the pool and in what order is not stated.
Only memory ablation: 64.2 -> 59.8 overall on MultiTQ, GPT-4o-mini.

evidence.quote: it causes a moderate performance drop from 64.2% to 59.8%, with larger reductions observed on multi-hop questions, from 40.3% to 26.1%.
the overall accuracy increases from 64.2% to 58.3%, while performance on multiple-entity questions drops sharply from 40.3% to 19.3%.
evidence.support_explanation: Text says 'increases' for a drop: presentation error.

evidence.quote: MemoTime with GPT-4-Turbo achieves an overall 77.9% Hit@1, surpassing TempAgent by 24.0% and outperforming all GPT-3.5 baselines by a large margin.
MemoTime boosts accuracy from as low as 1.3% to 61.4% on Qwen3-32B, achieving a 46.2 times relative gain.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 3 Qwen3-32B 61.4 conflicts with Table 1 Qwen3-32B 68.2 and the IO baseline of 1.3% looks like a format failure.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, MemoTime enables smaller models (e.g., Qwen3-4B) to achieve reasoning performance comparable to that of GPT-4-Turbo.
evidence.support_explanation: Table 3 shows Qwen3-4B 55.3 vs MemoTime GPT-4-Turbo 77.9; comparable only to IO/other baselines.

evidence.quote: MemoTime performs an average of 8.75 calls per question
evidence.support_explanation: Cost: LLM calls and 43.11 s per question for the whole system, not memory-specific.
Retained object is non-weight (memory, toolkit selection).

evidence.quote: MemoTime adopts a temporal-first pruning policy.
evidence.support_explanation: Main performance driver is temporal-first graph retrieval and decomposition; the memory is a secondary component.

gap.residue: Whether accumulated exemplars beat equal-size fixed exemplars
gap.stakes: Stability and efficiency of repeated temporal QA

claims.text: Experience memory adds stability and gains in temporal KG QA.
claims.result_denominator: Hits@1 overall 64.2 vs 59.8; evaluated-set size not stated
claims.allowed_conclusion: With one backbone on MultiTQ, removing memory lowers Hits@1 by 4.4 points; no evidence of accumulation over a stream or superiority to fixed exemplars.

claims.allowed_conclusion: Author-reported SOTA with internally inconsistent tables.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: Pipeline reaches high Hits@1 on two TKGQA benchmarks; memory-off lowers MultiTQ Hits@1 by 4.4 points in one setting.

G.reason: Real limitation (memoryless TKGQA, static exemplars) but memory neighbors (Reflexion, ExpeL, workflow memories) not examined; harness-RSI gap is secondary to the TKGQA gap.

M.reason: Typed, operator-filtered retrieval of exemplars for decomposition/toolkit/seed selection is a plausible mechanism; why accumulated exemplars beat fixed ones is asserted.

X.reason: Algorithms show read/write path with lambda weights and k; admission is an LLM sufficiency check, pruning/decay/rebalancing have no criteria, no versioning, rollback or stream order.

E.measurement.reason: Hits@1 against gold answers on MultiTQ/TimeQuestions is a trustworthy standard metric; marked down only for conflicting tables (see statistics).

E.causality.reason: Single store-off ablation (one dataset, one backbone, one run); no static-exemplar of equal size baseline (the stated gap), no write-gate or pruning ablation, no growth curve.

E.holdout.reason: Complete text and appendix do not say whether the pool is built on train, dev or the test stream, whether gold labels verify traces, or give a split between memory construction and evaluation.
search_scope: Appendix A, B, D (dataset stats, implementation)

E.statistics.reason: No seeds, intervals, significance, or evaluated-subset size (test splits are 54,584 and 3,237 but 43 s/question suggests subsampling); tables internally inconsistent.

E.cost.reason: Reports calls, depth, runtime for the whole system but no baseline-matched comparison and no memory-specific cost (growth, retrieval latency).
